detailed_description: The Markdown Preview tool lets you edit Markdown on one side and view sanitized HTML output on the other. The page starts with a sample document, updates the preview as the Markdown changes, and includes a copy action for the generated HTML. It is useful for drafting README sections, documentation snippets, notes, and formatted text before moving it into another editor. The renderer supports common Markdown patterns used by the site, but complex extensions can vary from platform to platform, so review the final result where you publish it.
usage_steps: Type or paste Markdown into the editor.
Watch the preview update beside the editor.
Review headings, lists, links, inline code, and code blocks.
Click Export HTML to copy the generated HTML.
Paste the HTML into your target workflow if needed.
Use Clear when you want to start from an empty editor.
usage_examples: Preview a README section before committing it.
Convert a short Markdown note into HTML for a CMS field.
Check whether code blocks and lists render as expected.
Draft documentation text while keeping a live formatted preview visible.

faqs.question: What does the Markdown Preview tool output?
faqs.answer: It shows a live HTML preview and lets you copy the generated HTML.

faqs.question: Can I clear the editor?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Clear button empties the Markdown input.

faqs.question: Does the preview support code blocks?
faqs.answer: Yes. The sample content includes inline code and fenced code blocks.

faqs.question: Will the output match GitHub exactly?
faqs.answer: Not always. Markdown extensions can differ by platform, so review the final rendering where you publish.

faqs.question: Is generated HTML sanitized?
faqs.answer: The page passes rendered Markdown through the site's sanitize helper before displaying it.
